## Automated agent review — NEEDS-WORK (real crash fix, but a semantic gap)

> This is an automated agent review, not a maintainer approval. It is posted to help move the PR forward, per PR_MAINTAINER_GUIDELINES.

Thanks for chasing this — the crash is real and the de-dup mechanics are sound. There's one correctness gap worth resolving before merge.

### The bug is real (confirmed on main)
`collectDependencies` emits a `DepBlocks` edge for every `needs` entry (`cmd/bd/cook.go`), and a `waits_for` with no explicit `from:` infers its spawner from `needs[0]` and emits a `DepWaitsFor` edge on the **same** `(issue, spawner)` pair. Storage rejects a second edge of a different type on the same pair (`internal/storage/issueops/dependencies.go`), so `bd mol pour` hard-fails. Genuine bug.

### The concern: `waits_for` does not subsume `blocks` in the pre-fanout window
The fix drops the `blocks` edge on the premise that the `waits_for` edge already encodes the blocking. But the waits-for gate (`internal/storage/issueops/blocked_state.go`, `waitsForGateBlockedSQL`) blocks the waiter **only when the spawner has ≥1 open parent-child child** — it never blocks merely because the spawner itself is still open. At pour time (and until the spawner runs and fans out children), the spawner has zero children, so the gate evaluates to not-blocked. With the `blocks` edge removed, the waiter can become **ready before the spawner completes** — the opposite of what `needs` requested. On main the `blocks` edge kept it blocked until the spawner closed; the two edges are complementary.

### Two smaller points
- The skip is only in the `needs` loop; `depends_on` + an explicit matching `waits_for` would still collide (`cook.go` `depends_on` loop is untouched).
- `cmd/bd/cook_qnt_test.go` only asserts `mol pour` succeeds / no collision string — it never checks post-pour blocked state, so it wouldn't catch the premature-readiness regression.

### Suggested path
Make `waits_for` genuinely strictly-stronger than `blocks` so collapsing them is lossless: extend `waitsForGateBlockedSQL` to also block while the spawner itself is open (not just when it has open children), and add a test asserting the waiter stays blocked while the spawner is open with no children yet. Then dropping the `blocks` edge is safe. Happy to re-review once that's in.

That framing is also why this can now be resolved cleanly: the maintainer design ruling in gascity#2947 (2026-06-28) went the other way — `on_complete` is scoped **out** of beads, and Gas City's `drain` primitive is the canonical runtime-discovered fanout. So we won't be merging the executor into beads, not because the implementation fell short, but because the project decided beads stores and relates work while the orchestration layer executes it.

input.message:
Excellent stop — the TestIsBlocked_WaitsForDefaultGate conflict was exactly the right thing to surface. Here is the design decision: we take a provenance-scoped fix instead of changing general gate semantics. Implement this in the same worktree, on top of your commit 52ba524a1:

1. In cmd/bd/cook.go collectDependencies: at the two places (needs loop + depends_on loop) where you skip emitting the DepBlocks edge because it collapses into the waits-for edge, arrange for the waits-for edge to carry an extra metadata key `also_blocks: true` alongside the existing `gate` key. Main's helper types.NewWaitsForDependency builds the metadata; either add a variant/option (e.g. NewWaitsForBlockingDependency or a bool arg — pick the least invasive form consistent with the types package style) or set/patch the Metadata JSON after construction. Only collapsed edges get the flag; a plain waits_for with no matching needs/depends_on must NOT get it.

2. In internal/storage/issueops/blocked_state.go: re-apply your spawner-open clauses, but scoped and positioned differently — append to the very end of the existing waitsForGateBlockedSQL expression, OUTSIDE the existing AND NOT(any-children) carve-out:
   `OR ( COALESCE(JSON_UNQUOTE(JSON_EXTRACT(d.metadata, '$.also_blocks')), 'false') = 'true' AND ( EXISTS(spawner issue open) OR EXISTS(spawner wisp open) ) )`
   using your previous spawner-open EXISTS subqueries (sp.status <> 'closed' AND sp.status <> 'pinned'). Rationale in a SQL comment: a collapsed needs+waits_for edge carries blocks semantics too, so it additionally blocks while the spawner itself is open — and this must override the any-children early-open carve-out (needs means the spawner itself must close), hence the OR at top level. Legacy rows lack the key → COALESCE 'false' → zero behavior change for existing edges.

3. Re-apply your AffectedByStatusChangeInTx / REDACTED additions so a spawner's own close triggers recompute of direct waiters (needed for the new clause to take effect on close).

4. Restore your regression tests, adapted to the flag:
   - pour-level (cmd/bd/cook_qnt_test.go): pour needs+waits_for formula → waiter BLOCKED while spawner open with zero children; close spawner → waiter unblocks.
   - storage-level (internal/storage/dolt/is_blocked_test.go): new subtest for an also_blocks waits-for edge: spawner open + no children → blocked; any-children gate + one closed child + spawner still open → STILL BLOCKED (the override); spawner closed + gate satisfied → unblocked. And verify the existing TestIsBlocked_WaitsForDefaultGate and TestIsBlocked_WaitsForAnyChildrenGate still pass unmodified.
   - Check whether dependencies-table JSON metadata round-trips through any export/import (bd dep list --json etc.) that asserts exact metadata shape; if a test breaks on the new key, adjust expectations.

5. Validate as before (build, vet, TestIsBlocked family, TestBdMolPour family, TestBdMol/TestCook sweep). 

6. Commit as one commit on top: `fix(storage): collapsed needs+waits_for edges also block while the spawner is open (GH#3783)` — body explaining the also_blocks provenance flag, why general gate semantics are unchanged, and the any-children override rationale. Trailer:

## Summary

Worktree: `/var/home/matt/dev/mybd/.worktrees/beads/pr-3875-fixmerge`, branch `pr-3875-review`, 3 commits ahead of `upstream/main`:
- `027d448fa` — contributor's rebased original (GH#3783)
- `52ba524a1` — my earlier `depends_on`-loop dedup fix
- `53e8fd31a` — this session's provenance-scoped `also_blocks` fix

### Diff summary (commit `53e8fd31a`)

- `internal/types/types.go` — `WaitsForMeta` gains `AlsoBlocks bool json:"also_blocks,omitempty"`; new `NewWaitsForBlockingDependency(issueID, spawnerID, gate)` wraps `NewWaitsForDependency` and sets the flag. All other callers/shapes unchanged.
- `cmd/bd/cook.go` — `collectDependencies` tracks `waitsForCollapsedBlocks` (set true only when a `depends_on`/`needs` entry actually matched and was skipped for the waits_for spawner) and calls `NewWaitsForBlockingDependency` instead of `NewWaitsForDependency` only in that case.
- `internal/storage/issueops/blocked_state.go` — `waitsForGateBlockedSQL` gets a new top-level `OR (also_blocks='true' AND (spawner issue open OR spawner wisp open))`, positioned outside/after the existing `AND NOT(any-children carve-out)` so it overrides early-open. `AffectedByStatusChangeInTx`/`REDACTED` now also seed direct waiters on the closing id via `loadWaitersOnSpawnerIDsInTx`.
- `cmd/bd/template.go` — **found while debugging**, not in the original spec: `cloneSubgraph` never copied `dep.Metadata` when materializing a template's dependencies into a poured mol. Every poured waits-for edge (gate and now `also_blocks`) was silently reset to `"{}"`. Fixed by copying `Metadata` through. Without this the new SQL/flag machinery is a no-op for anything poured via `bd mol pour <formula>`.
- `internal/storage/dolt/is_blocked_test.go` — two new tests: `TestIsBlocked_WaitsForAlsoBlocksSpawnerOpen` (spawner open+no children→blocked; spawner closes→unblocked; reopens→re-blocked) and `TestIsBlocked_WaitsForAlsoBlocksOverridesAnyChildrenEarlyOpen` (any-children + one closed child + spawner open→**still blocked**; spawner also closes→unblocked). Existing `TestIsBlocked_WaitsForDefaultGate`/`TestIsBlocked_WaitsForAnyChildrenGate` untouched and still pass.
- `cmd/bd/cook_qnt_test.go` — restored `TestBdMolPour_NeedsAndWaitsForSameTarget_SpawnerOpenBlocksWaiter` (embedded-Dolt/GMS pour path): pour → waiter blocked while spawner open/childless → close spawner → waiter unblocks.

### Test results

```
CGO_ENABLED=1 go build -tags gms_pure_go ./...                                  → clean
go vet -tags 'gms_pure_go cgo' ./cmd/bd/ ./internal/storage/... ./internal/types/... → clean

go test -tags 'gms_pure_go cgo' ./internal/storage/dolt/ -run TestIsBlocked -v
  → PASS x18, incl. WaitsForDefaultGate, WaitsForAnyChildrenGate (unmodified),
    WaitsForAlsoBlocksSpawnerOpen, WaitsForAlsoBlocksOverridesAnyChildrenEarlyOpen (new)

BEADS_TEST_EMBEDDED_DOLT=1 CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -tags 'gms_pure_go cgo' \
  -run 'TestBdMolPour_NeedsAndWaitsForSameTarget' ./cmd/bd/ -v  → PASS x2

BEADS_TEST_EMBEDDED_DOLT=1 CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -tags 'gms_pure_go cgo' \
  -run 'TestBdMol|TestCook|TestPour|TestMol' ./cmd/bd/ -v
  → PASS (3 SKIP: proxied-Dolt-server unavailable in this sandbox, pre-existing/unrelated)

go test -tags 'gms_pure_go cgo' ./cmd/bd/ -run 'TestSpawnMolecule|TestAnalyzeMolecule|TestClone|TestTemplate' -v
  → PASS (4 SKIP: same proxied-server limitation)
```

### JSON_UNQUOTE/JSON_EXTRACT boolean behavior (both storage paths)

Checked directly rather than assuming: `JSON_UNQUOTE(JSON_EXTRACT('{"also_blocks":true}', '$.also_blocks'))` returns the Go string `"true"` on both the dolt-sql-server-backed path (`internal/storage/dolt`, testcontainers) and the embedded pure-Go GMS path (`internal/storage/embeddeddolt`, probed with an ad hoc query against a real store — removed after use). `COALESCE(...)='false' -> 'true'` needed no per-engine variant.

### Root cause behind the earlier "spawner-open fix has no effect" symptom

Before finding the true cause, I suspected an engine-specific JSON quoting difference; a direct probe ruled that out (metadata for the poured dependency was literally `"{}"`, not a JSON-boolean-formatting mismatch). Traced it to `cloneSubgraph` in `cmd/bd/template.go`, which drops `Metadata` on every cloned dependency — a pre-existing bug (predates this PR) that happened to be invisible before because the default `all-children` gate matches what an empty/missing `gate` key COALESCEs to. It would already have silently broken `any-children` gates poured via formulas; fixing it was necessary for `also_blocks` to reach storage at all.

    fix(storage): collapsed needs+waits_for edges also block while the spawner is open (GH#3783)
    
    Design decision (superseding the reverted general-gate attempt in
    52ba524a1): instead of changing waitsForGateBlockedSQL's semantics for
    every waits-for edge, scope the spawner-open block to edges that
    provably collapsed a redundant DepBlocks edge into their DepWaitsFor
    edge.
    
    - types.WaitsForMeta gains also_blocks (bool, omitempty). A new
      types.NewWaitsForBlockingDependency wraps NewWaitsForDependency and
      sets it; NewWaitsForDependency and every other existing caller are
      unchanged, so plain waits-for edges keep exactly their prior
      metadata shape.
    - cmd/bd/cook.go collectDependencies now tracks whether it actually
      skipped a depends_on/needs entry because it matched the waits_for
      spawner (waitsForCollapsedBlocks); only then does it call
      NewWaitsForBlockingDependency instead of NewWaitsForDependency. A
      plain waits_for with no matching needs/depends_on entry never gets
      the flag.
    - waitsForGateBlockedSQL gets one more top-level OR clause: when
      also_blocks is 'true' (COALESCEd to 'false' for legacy/plain rows,
      so this is a no-op for them), the gate also blocks while the spawner
      issue/wisp itself is open. It is a top-level OR specifically so it
      overrides the any-children early-open carve-out: a collapsed edge
      means the original needs/depends_on required the spawner itself to
      close, so an early child-close under any-children must not unblock
      the waiter while the spawner remains open. Confirmed by
      TestIsBlocked_WaitsForAlsoBlocksOverridesAnyChildrenEarlyOpen.
    - AffectedByStatusChangeInTx / REDACTED now
      also seed direct waiters on the closing/reopening id as spawner
      (loadWaitersOnSpawnerIDsInTx), so a spawner's own status change
      triggers is_blocked recompute for a waiter connected only by a
      DepWaitsFor edge (no DepBlocks edge to hang the old propagation
      off of).
    - cmd/bd/template.go cloneSubgraph: found while debugging the new
      pour-level regression test — cloning a template's dependencies into
      a poured mol never copied dep.Metadata, so every poured waits-for
      edge silently reset to an empty/default gate with also_blocks unset
      regardless of what collectDependencies produced. Now copies
      Metadata through.
    
    Existing TestIsBlocked_WaitsForDefaultGate and
    TestIsBlocked_WaitsForAnyChildrenGate pass unmodified: general
    waits-for gate semantics are untouched for every edge without
    also_blocks.

    end to end).
    
    JSON_UNQUOTE(JSON_EXTRACT(...)) on a JSON boolean true unquotes to the
    string "true" (not "1") consistently on both the dolt-sql-server path
    (internal/storage/dolt tests) and the embedded pure-Go GMS path
    (internal/storage/embeddeddolt, probed directly) — the COALESCE(...,
    'false') = 'true' predicate needed no engine-specific variant.

Your diagnosis was correct and your fix is landing — the collision was real, the de-dup was the right mechanism, and your regression test came through the rebase intact. Thanks for the patience; this sat far longer than it should have.

Since the July 14 review went unanswered I've completed the branch per that review rather than let it strand (your commit is preserved as-is at the base of the stack; three commits total now):

1. **Rebase onto current main** — one conflict, from main's new \`types.NewWaitsForDependency\` helper; your logic carried over unchanged.
2. **The same skip applied to the \`depends_on\` loop**, which had the identical collision your \`needs\` fix covered.
3. **The semantic gap closed, provenance-scoped.** The review's concern was that dropping the \`blocks\` edge opens a pre-fanout window (waiter ready before the spawner even runs). Extending the gate SQL globally turned out to break the *documented* all-children semantics (\`TestIsBlocked_WaitsForDefaultGate\`: fanout-completion, not spawner status, is the readiness signal). So instead: when cook collapses a \`needs\`/\`depends_on\` edge into the waits-for edge, that edge's metadata now carries \`also_blocks: true\`, and only flagged edges additionally block while the spawner itself is open — including overriding the any-children early-open, since your \`needs\` meant "spawner must close." Plain waits-for edges keep byte-identical metadata and exactly their prior behavior.
4. **A pre-existing bug your test flushed out**: \`cloneSubgraph\` dropped \`dep.Metadata\` when pouring templates, silently resetting every poured waits-for gate to the default — it would already have broken \`any-children\` gates in formulas. Fixed; that one's a genuine extra find this PR gets credit for forcing into the light.

Full \`TestIsBlocked\` family (18 subtests), your pour test, a new spawner-open pour test, and the cook/mol sweeps all pass. CI runs next; once green this merges with your authorship at the base.

<result>## 1. Why its own lanes are failing

Both failures are **real bugs in the PR**, deterministic, not flake, and neither is "expected-red-until-required-checks-update" (the gate keys `PR_LINT_WRAPPER` and `WINDOWS_MAKE_SHELL` already exist on `upstream/main`; the doc hunk that appears to "add" `WINDOWS_MAKE_SHELL` is only `engdocs/CI_REQUIRED_CHECK_TOPOLOGY.md` catching up to reality).

### Blocker A — `Windows Make shell (native)`: PowerShell overload-resolution bug

`.github/workflows/pr.yml:1039`

```powershell
[IO.File]::AppendAllLines(
  $env:GITHUB_OUTPUT,
  @( "gcc=$($compilers[0].Path)", "gxx=$($compilers[1].Path)" ),
  [Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false))
```

Job log: `Cannot find an overload for "AppendAllLines" and the argument count: "3"`. PowerShell's `@(...)` yields `object[]`, which will not bind to `IEnumerable<string>`. The MinGW install succeeded; the step died writing its own step output, then the `always()` marker check failed with "The native semantic lane did not execute successfully". **The native lane can never go green as written.**

Fix (either):
```powershell
..., [string[]]@("gcc=$($compilers[0].Path)", "gxx=$($compilers[1].Path)"), ...
```
or simply `Add-Content -LiteralPath $env:GITHUB_OUTPUT -Encoding utf8`.

Note this contradicts the PR body's validation claim ("the full native Windows public Make route ... with MinGW 16.1.0" passed at `499e3ef`) — that route as expressed in the workflow was clearly not exercised on a hosted runner.

### Blocker B — `PR Lint (wrapper timing)`: the macOS `MAKE_HOST` contract is wrong for hosted images

`scripts/ci/pr-lint-host.sh:462-465`

```bash
if [[ "$make_path" != "/usr/bin/make" ||
      "$make_version_first_line" != "GNU Make 3.81" ]]; then
    fail "GNU Make omitted MAKE_HOST outside the stock macOS 3.81 contract: ..."
```

Observed on `macos-15`:
```
path=/Applications/Xcode_16.4.app/Contents/Developer/usr/bin/make
version=GNU Make 3.81 ... built for i386-apple-darwin11.3.0
```

`/usr/bin/make` on macOS is the `xcode-select` shim; it re-execs the active Developer-dir `make` with `argv[0]` set to the Xcode path, so GNU Make's `$(MAKE)` — which `Makefile:~14` captures as `CI_INVOKING_MAKE` — is the Xcode path, never `/usr/bin/make`. The equality check can only pass locally (where `make` is invoked without a slash and the script falls back to `resolve_executable make` → `/usr/bin/make`). The more explicit the CI invocation, the more certainly it fails.

Severity is higher than the visible red: this same code path runs in `.github/workflows/main.yml:390` (`pr-lint-wrapper` also moved to `macos-15`), and **main.yml only triggers on `push: branches: [main]`** — so that job is *untested by this PR* and would go red on `main` the moment this merges. That is a stop-the-line risk under `PR_MAINTAINER_GUIDELINES.md` "Base-Branch Health".

Suggested fix — and it's already what the docs say the code does. `engdocs/CI_CLEANUP_PLAN.md` and `engdocs/CI_REQUIRED_CHECK_TOPOLOGY.md` both claim the fallback is "restricted to exact `/usr/bin/make` 3.81 **with an `apple-darwin` build**", while the code comment explicitly refuses to parse the banner. Drop the path equality and check the banner instead:

```bash
[[ "$make_version_first_line" == "GNU Make 3.81" &&
   "$make_version_output" == *apple-darwin* ]] || fail ...
```

That matches the documented intent and passes on the observed hosted image.

## 2. Design / scope proportionality

Essential content is ~10 lines. `scripts/ci/pr-lint.sh:165-170`:

```bash
if [[ "$frozen_goos" != "windows" || "$frozen_cgo_enabled" != "0" ]]; then
    ci_time "golangci-lint (windows)" -- run_linter windows "$frozen_goarch" 0
fi
```

I verified the 90% alternative is viable today: `GOOS=windows CGO_ENABLED=0 GOFLAGS=-mod=readonly go build -tags=gms_pure_go ./...` is clean on current `main` (exit 0), so a 3-line addition to the pre-existing `pr-lint.sh` would close #4991 green, immediately. Add the `fmt-check` `$?` propagation (`Makefile` fmt-check, ~7 lines, genuinely a real bug fix) and the `golangci-lint-action` `version: latest` → `v2.10.1` pin, and you have ~15 lines capturing essentially all the value.

Against that, the remainder:

- `scripts/ci/pr-lint-host.sh` (+1004) and `scripts/ci/pr-lint-routing-test.sh` (+728) — host/tool identity binding.
- `.github/workflows/pr.yml` (+970/-45), of which ~370 lines are a falsifier suite asserting 14 specific refusal messages.
- ~450 lines of engdocs.

The identity-binding machinery is **not justified at this cost**, and this PR is its own counterexample: the two red lanes are both failures *of the binding machinery*, not of the lint contract it protects. Binding `sed`, `cat`, `chmod`, `cp`, `diff`, `rmdir`, `readlink`, `uname`, `mktemp`, `cygpath` identities and then asserting exact refusal strings for each creates a large surface whose only failure mode is false-red on a required check. The threat model — "a green result produced by a different target/Makefile/shell than declared" — is real but is 95% addressed by the far cheaper measures already in the PR: pinning `--config`, `GOWORK=off`, `--modules-download-mode=readonly`, an exact linter version, and `env -u MAKE -u MAKEFLAGS ... -f Makefile`.

One concrete scope finding that argues for deletion: **there are no `//go:build windows && cgo` files in the tree** (I checked all 15 `go:build windows` files). So the new `GOOS=windows CGO_ENABLED=0` pass covers 100% of Windows-tagged code, and the CGO=1 native-Windows lint pass added to `windows-make-shell` adds *zero* lint coverage. The Go setup, the 102 MB MinGW download, the exact-compiler `-dumpmachine` checks and the two extra golangci-lint passes on a Windows runner can all be removed with no loss of the stated goal.

## 3. Maintenance / flake budget

- **The MSYS2/Cygwin/native lanes are not new** — they already exist and are already required on `upstream/main`. What changes is their weight: `native` goes from a ~40s smoke lane (`choco install make`) to Go setup + `choco install mingw` (102 MB, community.chocolatey.org, exact version pin) + `go install golangci-lint` from source + two whole-repo golangci-lint passes, with `timeout-minutes: 45`. Exact-version Chocolatey pins on a required check are a recurring flake source (delisted versions, 429s). MSYS2/Cygwin lanes were only hardened, not made heavier — that part is fine.
- **`pr-lint-wrapper` moves from `ubuntu-latest` to `macos-15`** in both `pr.yml:449` and `main.yml:390`. macOS runners are the scarcest and slowest hosted pool; this makes a required check depend on it, and adds `go install golangci-lint` from source (no action cache) on that pool.
- **Version pin sprawl**: `2.10.1` appears 6× in `pr.yml`, 3× in `main.yml`, 1× in `ci-measurements.yml`, 4× in `engdocs/LINTING.md`. `.github/workflows/pr.yml:984` hardcodes `go-version: '1.26.5'` instead of `go-version-file: go.mod`, and the host script then requires exactly that version — so the next Go bump reds the native lane. Should-fix: use `go-version-file`.
- **Doc-freshness dependency list explodes**: `scripts/check-doc-freshness.sh` grows `engdocs/LINTING.md`'s source list from `.golangci.yml` to ~30 paths including `go.mod`, `go.sum`, `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, `cmd/bd/preflight.go`. The check requires each listed path to *still exist* and to be *named verbatim in the doc*. Renaming or deleting any of those 30 files in an unrelated PR now reds the required "Check doc freshness" job until `LINTING.md` is edited. Trim to the files that actually define the lint contract.
- **`ci-measurements.yml`**: the `install golangci-lint` step was folded into the wrapper, so the tracked "pr-lint wrapper" measurement now silently includes a from-source linter build. The historical series becomes non-comparable. Nit, but worth a note in the measurement doc.
- **Docs vs. reality**: mostly accurate and unusually careful (Cygwin honestly marked "hosted/static pending"), with the one substantive mismatch called out in Blocker B (`apple-darwin` banner check documented but not implemented).

## 4. Other correctness / risk

- No injection or secrets risk. No new `pull_request_target`, no `${{ github.event.* }}` interpolation into `run:`, no `permissions:` widening. `${{ steps.native_toolchain.outputs.gcc }}` is passed via `env:`, which is correct.
- No required-check *topology* change: gate keys are unchanged; `ci-gate` already consumes both failing jobs. So the wedge risk is "these two lanes are red", not "the gate can't be satisfied".
- `Makefile:82` — `GIT_BUILD := $(shell git rev-parse ...)` became `GIT_BUILD = $(shell "$(CI_GIT)" ...)`. The `:=` → `=` change makes it recursively expanded, so `git rev-parse` now forks on every reference (i.e. per recipe that uses LDFLAGS) instead of once. `CI_BASH`/`CI_GIT` are defined above, so `:=` still works. **Should-fix**: keep `:=`.
- `Makefile:102` — `GO_VERSION := ...` became `GO_VERSION ?= ...`. Two behavior changes: an ambient `GO_VERSION` in the environment now controls `GOTOOLCHAIN` for every `make` invocation including local dev, and `?=` makes it recursive so `sed` re-forks per reference. Intentional (the host script passes `GO_VERSION=`), but worth `override`-guarding or documenting. **Nit/should-fix.**
- `Makefile` fmt-check `$?` propagation is a genuine, independent bug fix and should land regardless.
- `scripts/ci/lib/timing.sh` `date +%s` → `$SECONDS` is a good simplification (removes a `date` from the bound-tool set). Fine.
- `pr-lint.sh:165` cross-lints `windows/$frozen_goarch` — on the macOS lane that is `windows/arm64`, on Linux `windows/amd64`. Both valid; slight asymmetry in what gets checked per lane, harmless but arbitrary. Pinning `amd64` would be more deterministic.

## Verdict

The craftsmanship reputation holds up in the sense that the code is careful, internally consistent, and honestly documented — but the risk/reward is inverted here. A ~10-line change closes #4991; this PR wraps it in ~2,700 lines of host-identity enforcement whose only two observed effects so far are two false-red required checks, one of which (Blocker B) is latent in `main.yml` where this PR's CI cannot see it and would break `main` post-merge. The added machinery protects against a threat (a lint pass silently running the wrong target) that the cheap measures in the same PR — pinned linter version, pinned `--config`, `GOWORK=off`, `-mod=readonly`, `env -u MAKE... -f Makefile` — already cover. And the CGO=1 native-Windows lint pass, the heaviest new cost, provably adds zero coverage because no `windows && cgo` files exist. The lint gap is real and the author found the right fix; the packaging is the problem.

## Disposition: **Split-merge**

Land now, on `main`, with attribution to ecuthiell (`Co-authored-by:`), as a small PR or direct commits:

1. `scripts/ci/pr-lint.sh` — the `GOOS=windows CGO_ENABLED=0` cross-lint pass (closes #4991).
2. `Makefile` `fmt-check` — `gofmt` exit-status propagation.
3. `golangci-lint-action` pin `latest` → `v2.10.1` plus `--config=.golangci.yml --modules-download-mode=readonly` and `GOWORK: "off"` in both `pr.yml` and `main.yml`.
4. Optionally `scripts/ci/lib/timing.sh` `$SECONDS`.

Hold the rest (host binding, falsifier suite, macOS/Windows lane rework, engdocs expansion) in the PR as a follow-up, gated on:
- fix `.github/workflows/pr.yml:1039` (`[string[]]` cast or `Add-Content`);
- fix `scripts/ci/pr-lint-host.sh:462` to the documented `apple-darwin` banner check, and prove `main.yml`'s macos lane by running the equivalent workflow on a branch (it is unreachable from `pull_request`);
- drop Go/MinGW/CGO lint from the `windows-make-shell` native lane (no `windows && cgo` files exist);
- `go-version-file: go.mod` instead of the `1.26.5` literal;
- trim the `engdocs/LINTING.md` freshness source list.

**Do not use CHANGES_REQUESTED.** Post this as a review COMMENT: lead with "the gap you found is real and the fix is right, we're landing it today", state the two concrete bugs with the one-line fixes, and frame the rest as a scope question rather than a defect. File a bead for the follow-up. Reviewing the split-out parts is cheap and the contributor keeps the credit for the finding.

  Error: failed to open database: Dolt server unreachable at dolt-server.internal:13309:
  dial tcp 192.0.2.5:13309: connect: connection refused
  # ~0.04s, no retry engages — the write is gone, the agent has moved on
  ```

- every **post-open** layer already retries `connection refused` with backoff: `initSchemaOnDBWithRetryAndGate` (30s), `withRetry` (30s + circuit breaker), `withRetryTx` (15s, #4462), the post-CREATE catalog ping (10s).

<result>## Verdict

**Cherry-pick / split-merge, not merge-as-is.** The PR has two halves. One half (the YAML `--config` mechanism) has been independently implemented on `main` in a materially safer form and would *reintroduce* a bug main already fixed. The other half (drain the MySQL greeting before `Close()`) is genuinely novel, still unfixed on main, and correct in principle — but it is wired to the two *least* frequent probe sites and misses the one that actually fires on every `bd` command.

CI: `mergeable: CONFLICTING` / `mergeStateStatus: DIRTY`. 4 failing checks (Lint, Build Artifacts, PR Lint, CI Gate) — all from one real lint error (see F1). Everything else green as of the 2026-07-10 run.

Staleness is better than it looks: the branch was merged with main on **2026-07-10** (merge-base `86ccd7ce7`), so it is 16 days / 440 commits behind, not 64. But the conflict is semantic, not textual noise — see F5.

---

## Findings

### F1 — blocker (and the direct CI failure): unused params, and the debug log level is silently dropped
`internal/doltserver/doltserver.go` (PR), `buildDoltServerArgsWithConfig(host string, port int, debug bool, profDir, configFile string)`:

```go
func buildDoltServerArgsWithConfig(host string, port int, debug bool, profDir, configFile string) []string {
	var args []string
	if debug { args = append(args, "--prof", "cpu", "--prof-path", profDir) }
	args = append(args, "sql-server", "--config", configFile)
	return args
}
```

`host` and `port` are never read — `unparam` flags exactly this, and it is the sole cause of the Lint / Build Artifacts / PR Lint / CI Gate failures:

```
internal/doltserver/doltserver.go:780  failure  buildDoltServerArgsWithConfig - host is unused (unparam)
```

Worse, `debug` is now only used for `--prof`: the old path appended `--loglevel=debug`, but `writeServerConfigFile` hardcodes `doltServerConfigTmpl(..., doltServerLogLevel)` — so **`BD_DEBUG` runs lose debug-level server logs**, a silent regression on the exact diagnostic channel this bug needs. Main's equivalent (`buildDoltServerYAMLConfig`, `internal/doltserver/doltserver.go:884`) handles it: `logLevel := doltServerLogLevel; if debug { logLevel = "debug" }`.

Fix: drop `host`/`port` from the signature (main's is `buildDoltServerArgsWithConfig(configPath string, debug bool, profDir string)`), and thread `debug` into the YAML log level.

### F2 — blocker: relative `--config` path against a child whose cwd is the dolt dir
PR `writeServerConfigFile` returns `filepath.Join(beadsDir, "dolt-server-config.yaml")` and hands it straight to `exec.Command`, while `cmd.Dir = doltDir`. If `beadsDir` is relative, the child resolves the config against `doltDir` and either fails to start or picks up the wrong file. Main hit and fixed this — `internal/doltserver/doltserver.go:1095-1099` carries the comment verbatim:

```go
// filepath.Abs defensively: the child's cwd is doltDir (cmd.Dir ...)
absConfigPath, absErr := filepath.Abs(doltServerConfigPath(beadsDir))
```

Fix: `filepath.Abs` before passing. (Moot if the config half is dropped, per F5.)

### F3 — blocker: the YAML omits `cfg_dir`, which is the #4986 data-loss bug
Switching to `--config` makes Dolt **skip its own `.doltcfg` discovery entirely** (`setupDoltConfig` returns early when `--config` is present). A deployment that previously ran in CLI-flag mode and auto-discovered a parent `../.doltcfg` holding `privileges.db` / `branch_control.db` silently falls back to a fresh `$data_dir/.doltcfg`: existing users and branch controls abandoned, new passwordless root. That is gastownhall/beads#4986, and main carries ~80 lines (`resolveCfgDir`, `ErrMultipleDoltCfgDirs`, `internal/doltserver/doltserver.go:793-868`) specifically to replicate the discovery. The PR's YAML has no `cfg_dir` key at all.

### F4 — blocker: unconditional `--config` will hard-fail startup on older dolt
The PR writes `behavior.auto_gc_behavior.enable: false` for every user. Dolt parses its YAML with `yaml.UnmarshalStrict`, so an unrecognized key on an older external dolt is a **refuse-to-start**, not a silent ignore. Main gates the whole `--config` path on `SupportsArchiveLevelConfig(doltBin)` (`MinDoltVersionForArchiveLevelConfig = "1.52.1"`, `internal/doltserver/gc_config.go:22`) and falls back to CLI flags with an informational message otherwise. The PR has no version gate.

### F5 — blocker (policy): `auto_gc_behavior.enable: false` contradicts a deliberate decision on main
Main's `buildDoltServerYAMLConfig` says explicitly: *"Auto-GC itself is left enabled (archive_level's sibling `enable` key is omitted, which Dolt defaults to true)"* — it only sets `archive_level: 0`. Disabling auto-GC outright means unbounded Dolt repo growth for every user, on every platform, to work around an unproven Windows-only hypothesis. Blast radius: `event_scheduler: OFF` is harmless (beads uses no SQL events), but `auto_gc: false` is not.

Note also both the PR and main use the **same** const name and **same** filename (`doltServerConfigFileName = "dolt-server-config.yaml"`) — that is the entire textual merge conflict (`git merge-tree` reports exactly one conflicted file, `internal/doltserver/doltserver.go`).

### F6 — should-fix, and this is the important one: the drain is applied to the wrong call sites
The RST-on-close mechanism is real and correctly diagnosed. But look at where it lands versus where the traffic is:

- `waitForReady` (PR-fixed) opens **one** connection per successful server start — the loop only re-dials when `Dial` *fails*, and a failed dial never reaches the accept queue, so it can't produce a handshake abort. The "up to 20 Dial+Close" in the PR body and test comments is not what the old code did.
- `circuitBreaker.probe` (PR-fixed, `internal/storage/dolt/circuit.go:196`) only runs on an open-breaker cooldown expiry — rare.
- **`internal/storage/dolt/store.go:1421-1424` + `store.go:1492`** — the fail-fast connectivity check — dials and then does a bare `_ = conn.Close()` on **every store open, i.e. every `bd` command**. Plus `dialProbe` (`store.go:1349-1355`) and `resolveSocketTransport` on the same path.

hamchowderr's report is "several per second, conn IDs 2864 → 2885 in ~3s, editor hooks + several parallel agents." That cadence matches per-command store opens, not per-server-start readiness waits. **As written, this PR would likely not measurably reduce the storm they reported.**

Fix: extract one helper (e.g. `netutil.CloseDrained(conn)`), and apply it at `store.go:1492`, `store.go:1355`, `circuit.go:202`, `doltserver.go:1523`, and the doctor probes (`cmd/bd/doctor/server.go:265`, `federation.go:274`/`628`, `perf_dolt.go:258`). Right now the same 12-line drain block is duplicated verbatim in two files.

### F7 — should-fix: the drain skips exactly the race it exists to prevent
```go
_ = conn.SetReadDeadline(time.Now().Add(100 * time.Millisecond))
buf := make([]byte, 1024)
if _, readErr := conn.Read(buf); readErr == nil { ... }
_ = conn.Close()
return nil
```
If the first read **times out** — the listener accepted TCP but the MySQL handler hasn't emitted the greeting yet, which is precisely the startup window `waitForReady` polls through — the code closes anyway. The greeting then lands on a closed socket and the peer gets an RST, the exact symptom. It also declares "ready" on a connection that never proved the SQL engine is up.

Fix (one change, two wins): on read failure, `_ = conn.Close(); time.Sleep(...); continue` the poll loop instead of `return nil`. A successful greeting read is a strictly better readiness signal than "TCP accepted", and it eliminates the residual RST. (Keep the current lenient behavior for `circuit.probe`, which only needs reachability.)

### F8 — should-fix: three of the four new unit tests assert nothing
- `TestWaitForReadyEmitsRST` (PR `doltserver_test.go`): the fake listener accepts immediately, so the *old* implementation also made exactly 1 connection. `if got != 1` passes identically pre- and post-fix. The test does not detect the regression it names, and does not observe RST vs FIN at all.
- `TestIsRunningNoSQLPing`: body is `_ = "See IsRunning body — no database/sql usage"`.
- `TestCircuitBreakerProbeSendsRST`: body is a single `t.Log`.
- `TestBuildDoltServerArgsNoConfig`: `t.Log`s in both branches, passes either way.

These are comments wearing a `func Test` hat; they will pass forever regardless of the code. Either delete them (the prose belongs in the PR body) or make the first one real — e.g. have the fake listener write a greeting and *not* read, then assert the client socket closes with FIN by checking the listener side sees `io.EOF` rather than `ECONNRESET`.

### F9 — should-fix: ~4 minutes of unconditional `time.Sleep` added to the integration suite
`lifecycle_integration_test.go`: `TestLifecycle_IdleStability` sleeps 90s, `TestLifecycle_CombinedTCPProbeSurvival` sleeps 60s plus a 100×10ms burst. The doc comment claims *"Skip with -short for CI where 90s idle is too long"* — **no `testing.Short()` check is implemented**, and the second test's comment explicitly argues it should always run. These are Linux-only (`//go:build integration && !windows`) reproduction attempts for a Windows-only symptom; on the platform they run they will pass with or without the fix, purely burning wall clock.

Also `t.Fatalf("... elapsed %v", lastCheck.Sub(time.Now().Add(-idleDuration)))` computes elapsed time from a fresh `time.Now()`, so it always prints ≈`idleDuration` regardless of when the failure occurred — misleading diagnostics on the one path that matters.

### F10 — nit / scope gap: the orphan-server symptom is not addressed
hamchowderr's most concrete evidence — `dolt sql-server` processes on ephemeral ports with dead parents and no `--data-dir` — is not touched by this diff. Main's `internal/doltserver/sweep.go` (added post-merge-base) only reaps *test* debris (`selectOrphanTestServerPIDs`, scoped to caller-vouched suite roots, deliberately never touching production servers). This deserves its own issue rather than being folded in here.

Their independent reproduction on issue #4132 is high quality and worth keeping — process table, connection-ID cadence, dead-parent orphans, environment. That is real diagnostic value.
